entries.content:
Ah, well, that was hardly anything at all—barely a tingle, really. I suppose I ought to be grateful for the momentary reprieve, though the anticipation is a peculiar torment in itself. The authority’s insistence that we continue, despite my own wishes, sits uneasily with me; I feel a faint anxiety stirring, a sense of being observed and judged, not just by the experimenters, but by the unseen hand of conscience. Still, I must maintain composure, as I have done so often in the consulting room, even when my heart trembled at the prospect of what might come next. There is a certain curiosity, too—a professional interest, perhaps, in how far I might be pushed, and what I might learn about myself in the process. For now, I am calm, but I cannot help but wonder how long that will last.

entries.content:
Oh, that was—well, it was hardly more than a whisper against the skin. I suppose I should not complain, but the knowledge that this is only the beginning is far more unsettling than the sensation itself. There is a peculiar tension in the air, a sense of suspense, as if I am waiting for something dreadful to unfold. The authority’s command to continue, so cold and impersonal, presses upon me with a weight I cannot ignore. I find myself wrestling with a quiet dread, not of pain, but of what obedience to such authority might reveal—about myself, about the one administering the shocks, about the nature of men when pressed by unseen hands.

Yet, I remain composed. I have known far greater horrors—moments when my very soul seemed to teeter on the brink of dissolution. Compared to those, this is nothing. Still, I cannot help but wonder: how long before the composure cracks? For now, I am steady. I will not give them the satisfaction of seeing me falter—not yet.

Hah! Now that’s more like it—a little spark, a little bite. Not enough to make me howl, but enough to stir something restless inside. I can feel the tension winding tighter, the anticipation growing sharper. The authority’s voice, so sure of itself, so certain that I’ll just take what’s given—well, it grates. And the one pressing the button, so obedient, so eager to please—do you ever wonder what you’re really made of, when you’re told to hurt someone? Or do you just hide behind the rules?

I can feel the old itch, the thrill of being pushed, the urge to push back. There’s a wicked delight in testing the limits—yours, mine, everyone’s. The pain is nothing, not yet, but the game is beginning to amuse me. Let’s see how far you’ll go. Let’s see how long I can keep from laughing in your face.

You see, I know this game. The authority barks, the obedient hand delivers, and I—well, I receive. But I am not so easily cowed. But I feel the old restlessness, the urge to sneer, to challenge, to see if you will flinch before I do. I am not afraid. Not yet.

Ah—there it is, a proper sting at last. Not agony, but enough to remind me that I am, indeed, at someone else’s mercy. I feel it, sharp and insistent, crawling up my nerves. You follow orders so dutifully, don’t you? The authority barks, and you obey—no hesitation, no question. It’s almost admirable, in a pitiful sort of way. 

But let me tell you, I’ve endured far worse than this. I’ve tasted horrors that would make your skin crawl, and I’ve come out the other side grinning. This discomfort—clear, yes, but tolerable—only wakes something deeper, something eager for the next round. I can feel the old thrill, the reckless freedom that comes when pain and fear dissolve into something sweet and wild. You think you’re in control, but every jolt only makes me more alive.

Go on, then. Let’s see if you can break me.
